- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates upside; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), especially in 30-day horizon; apply a 1–3% downward correction to peak values.
- Forecast mean tends to lag true outcome by 1–3 days; adjust for 1–2 day lag in 30d horizon by slightly increasing early forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mid-range values.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
